 Is your meat processing business adequately insured for modern risks? 
 Back Back Why traditional insurance thinking may no longer be enough 
 Australia's meat and poultry industry faces an evolving risk landscape. Emerging threats including cybercrime, biosecurity events, product contamination, regulatory scrutiny and supply chain disruption are creating exposures that can significantly impact profitability, reputation and business continuity. For many businesses, the key question is whether their insurance program is designed to respond to the risks they face today. 
 The new risk environment 
 Meat and poultry businesses operate within complex, interconnected supply chains where a single disruption can create significant financial consequences. Disease outbreaks, cyber incidents, equipment breakdowns and regulatory actions can affect production continuity and business performance. 
 Product recall: a multi-million-dollar exposure 
 Product recalls can generate substantial direct and indirect costs, including product withdrawal, customer notification, crisis management, brand damage and lost revenue. Review whether existing product liability and recall policies adequately address these exposures. 
 Business interruption is not just a property risk 
 Modern business interruption losses increasingly arise from non-property events such as disease outbreaks, supply chain disruption, cyber incidents and utility failures. Insurance structures should reflect these changing realities.
 Governance matters more than ever 
 Insurers increasingly assess governance, biosecurity management, cybersecurity controls, incident response planning and executive oversight when evaluating risk. Strong governance can improve resilience and insurance outcomes. 
 Common Coverage Gaps 
 Businesses should regularly review product recall, cyber liability, environmental liability, directors and officers liability, machinery breakdown and supply chain interruption coverages to identify potential gaps. 
 Looking ahead 
 The most resilient organisations will combine proactive risk management with a strategic insurance program. Insurance should be viewed as part of a broader business resilience framework rather than a compliance exercise.
